Aaron is the target of the rebels' complaint and is told to bring his censer to the Tent of Meeting with the others. After the LORD threatens the congregation a second time, he takes fire from the altar and incense, runs into the assembly, and makes atonement. He stands between the dead and the living, and the plague stops.

Dathan, son of Eliab of Reuben, joins Korah's rebellion and refuses Moses' summons, saying 'We won't come up.' He accuses Moses of bringing them out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill them and of making himself a prince. He stands at his tent door with his wife, sons, and little ones before the ground swallows them all alive.

Abiram, son of Eliab of Reuben, joins Korah's rebellion and, with Dathan, refuses to come when Moses summons him. He complains that Moses has not brought them into a land with fields and vineyards as an inheritance. He and his household are swallowed alive by the earth into Sheol.

Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, is told by the LORD to take the censers out of the burning and scatter the fire away from the camp. He beats the bronze censers into a covering for the altar. This serves as a memorial that no stranger outside Aaron's offspring should burn incense before the LORD.

The LORD's glory appears to the congregation, and he tells Moses and Aaron to separate so he can consume the people in a moment, but he relents after they plead. He instructs Moses to have the people move away from the rebels' tents, and he judges the rebels by opening the earth and sending fire on the 250 incense offerers. When the congregation complains the next day, he again threatens to consume them and sends a plague that kills 14,700 before atonement stops it.

Korah's company, including the 250 princes of renown, gathers against Moses and Aaron and takes censers with fire and incense to stand before the LORD at the Tent of Meeting. The earth swallows Korah's men with their households and goods. Fire from the LORD devours the 250 men who offered incense.

Some Israelites join the rebellion, while the rest are warned to depart from the rebels' tents and flee when the earth swallows them. The next day the congregation complains that Moses and Aaron have killed the LORD's people. A plague then kills 14,700 before Aaron's atonement stops it.

Each of the 250 rebels and Aaron is told to bring a censer with fire and incense before the LORD. After the fire destroys the rebels, the bronze censers are declared holy because they were offered before the LORD. They are beaten into plates as an altar covering, serving as a sign and memorial. Aaron's censer is later used to make atonement during the plague.

l: earth swallowing the rebels, Numbers, Chapter 16
s: As Moses finishes saying that the LORD would make a new thing, the ground splits and the earth opens its mouth. It swallows Korah's men, Dathan, Abiram, their households, and all their goods, who go down alive into Sheol before the earth closes over them. The Israelites around them flee at their cry for fear of being swallowed too.

A plague begins among the congregation after they complain that Moses and Aaron killed the LORD's people, because wrath has gone out from the LORD. It kills 14,700, in addition to those who died in the matter of Korah. It stops when Aaron makes atonement with incense, standing between the dead and the living.

The rebellion is a challenge by Korah, Dathan, Abiram, On, and 250 princes to the authority of Moses and Aaron, claiming the whole congregation is holy. It ends in judgment, with the earth swallowing the leaders' households and fire consuming the 250 incense offerers. The aftermath includes the altar covering made from their censers as a memorial and a further complaint by the congregation that leads to a plague.

The LORD instructs Moses to collect twelve rods, one from each prince of the children of Israel, with Aaron's name written on Levi's rod, and to lay them before the covenant in the Tent of Meeting so that the rod of the chosen man will bud and the murmuring will cease. Moses does so, and the next day Aaron's rod has sprouted, budded, blossomed, and borne ripe almonds. Moses brings all the rods out, and each man takes his own. The LORD commands that Aaron's rod be put back before the covenant as a token against the rebellious, to end their complaining so they do not die. The children of Israel respond in fear, saying they perish and that everyone who approaches the LORD's tabernacle dies.

The LORD commands Moses to gather twelve rods and lay them before the covenant, declaring that the rod of the man he chooses will bud and that this will make the Israelites' murmuring cease. He then orders Aaron's rod put back before the covenant as a token against the children of rebellion, so that they not die.

Moses carries out the LORD's instructions exactly: he speaks to the Israelites, receives the twelve rods, and lays them up in the Tent of the Testimony. The next day he finds Aaron's rod budded, brings all the rods out to the people, and puts Aaron's rod back as commanded.
Aaron's name is written on the rod of Levi, representing the house of Levi. His rod is the one that miraculously sprouts, buds, blossoms, and bears almonds, marking him as the man the LORD chose.

The children of Israel, through their princes, each give Moses a rod, and afterward each man takes back his own rod when they look at them. They then cry out in fear that they perish and are undone, saying that everyone who approaches the LORD's tabernacle dies.

Aaron's rod, representing the house of Levi, is laid up among the others before the LORD and by the next day has sprouted, budded, produced blossoms, and borne ripe almonds. The LORD has it put back before the covenant to be kept as a token against the children of rebellion.

l: rods (of the twelve princes), Numbers, Chapter 17
s: Twelve rods, one from each prince according to their fathers' houses, are collected and laid up before the LORD in the Tent of the Testimony. Only Aaron's rod buds; the rest are brought out and each man takes his own.
The Tent of Meeting, also called the Tent of the Testimony, is the place where the rods are laid before the covenant, where the LORD meets with Moses. Aaron's rod is kept there afterward as a token.

l: murmuring and complaining of the Israelites, Numbers, Chapter 17
s: The LORD intends the budding of the chosen rod to make the Israelites' murmurings against Moses cease. He says Aaron's rod is to be kept as a token to end their complaining so that they not die, and the people respond with fear of perishing.

The LORD addresses Aaron and his sons, making them responsible for bearing the iniquity of the sanctuary and the priesthood, while the Levites are joined to them to serve the Tent of Meeting but may not approach the sanctuary vessels or altar. The LORD gives Aaron, his sons, and his daughters the wave offerings, most holy things, first fruits, devoted things, and firstborn offerings as a perpetual portion, with firstborn humans and unclean animals to be redeemed for five shekels. Aaron is told he will have no land inheritance, since the LORD is his portion. The Levites receive all of Israel's tithe as their inheritance in return for their service, and the children of Israel are barred from approaching the Tent of Meeting lest they bear sin and die. Speaking to Moses, the LORD instructs that the Levites must offer a tithe of the tithe as a wave offering to Aaron the priest, after which the rest is theirs to eat anywhere without incurring sin.

The LORD speaks to Aaron and Moses, assigning the priestly duties and giving Aaron's house the wave offerings and holy things as a portion forever. He declares himself Aaron's portion and inheritance, gives the tithe to the Levites, and sets the rule of the tithe of the tithe.

Aaron is told that he and his sons will bear the iniquity of the sanctuary and the priesthood and guard the altar and what is within the veil. He receives the wave offerings, most holy things, first fruits, and firstborn offerings as a portion, but is given no inheritance in the land because the LORD is his inheritance. He is also to receive the LORD's wave offering from the Levites' tithe.

Aaron's sons are to serve with him before the Tent of the Testimony and bear the iniquity of the priesthood. They share the portion of holy things, with every male eating of the most holy things, and their daughters share the wave offerings as well.
